a vacuum sealer with a marinating container will give you MUCH lower marinating times. like an hour or 2. I marinated some 1-1/2"+ strips in teriyaki, worstershire, and Head Country. the meat was TOTALLY permeated thru and thru.
Huh, I totally forgot about vacuum sealers. Do you recommend them overall or find you only use it so often?

mine stays out on the counter always. buy a block of cheese, use what you want, put it in a longer bag than you need. re-use the bag until the cheese is gone. vac sealed food will last longer. i bought a box of 5 or 6 rolls of the bags for pretty cheap at wally world. don't waste the money on the name brand shit. hell, my vacuum sealer is even a knock-off.

i buy family pack size EVERYTHING, and break up, bag and vacuum pack into individual meal size. it's much better than just putting something in a ziplock, and purging the air. frozen meat no longer has any freezer burn, and keeps longer. you can even do soups in the bags if you freeze them first in a bowl. i have 16oz of ricotta in the freezer now, b/c walmart is a dick, selling only 15oz, or 32oz, when i need 16oz.

i found a couple of the round canisters at garage sales for $2-3, and found a square marinating container for $2. i had to pony up amazon retail for the tube to connect to the hard plastics. a whole $6. the round containers are great for fruits and veggies, sauces, really anything perishable. take what you want or need, then put it back under vacuum. if you've got any mason jars, there's an adapter for that. your lid on the jar, then the adapter sucks the air out of the jar, leaving your lid on it. move on to the next jar. note: this is NOT the same as canning, but will extend the shelf life of anything you put in there.

TL;DR the marinating container is the bees knees, and the bags are of more value than you realize once you start using them
